# Nomameshi

> Your local meal companion. Photograph a foreign-language menu and an AI translates it with cuisine context, generates a table-spread visualization, and surfaces country-specific food culture tips. For slow nomads who want to eat where locals eat.

## What this is

Nomameshi (のまめし) is an iOS + web app for travelers who prefer neighborhood taverns over tourist restaurants. It pairs OCR-grade menu translation with food-culture context so the entire "waiting for your meal" experience becomes enjoyable.

- Frontend: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript
- AI (translation): Gemini 2.5 Flash (`gemini-2.5-flash`)
- AI (image): Gemini 2.5 Flash Image (`gemini-2.5-flash-image`)
- Mobile: Capacitor 8 (iOS)
- Hosting: Vercel (SSR + serverless API routes)
- Design: Pencil.dev (`design/nomameshi.pen`)

API keys are server-only; clients never see them. IP-based rate limiting (10 req/min). Translation history kept in localStorage (max 20 entries — a lightweight travel log).

## Audience

- Slow nomads (multi-week / multi-month overseas stays)
- Travelers who prefer local cafeterias, bars, taverns over chain restaurants
- People treating "menu translation" as a daily-life tool, not a travel utility

## What this is NOT

- Not a phrasebook or general-purpose translator — it specializes in food/menu context
- Not a restaurant discovery service — bring your own restaurant, the app helps you order
- Not an Android app (currently) — iOS via Capacitor + web via Vercel
- Not a calorie or nutrition tracker — see [tonton](https://github.com/DELAxGithub/tonton) for that
